facilities.notes: SIEN contact page (updated April 9, 2025) lists three network staff: Anne Pfaff (Program Manager), Sarah Wakamiya (Data Manager), Kelly Martin (Physical Scientist). About-us page says the network is hiring an ecologist, logistics coordinator and science communicator; Linda Mutch is no longer listed. Steve Fancy and Thomas Philippi are national NPS-IM figures and do not appear on nps.gov/im or the SIEN pages fetched. [verifier] Linda Mutch absent from current staff list (stale); no fetched page states who succeeded her, so current_holder_key left null.

No current NPS staff page names the superintendent; Clay Jordan is named Superintendent as contact on a USAJobs SEKI vacancy (Resources Management and Sciences Chief) whose qualifications deadline was 04/20/2026, and an archived NPS release (Sept 2020) records his selection starting Nov 8, 2020. That chief-of-science position was vacant/being filled in 2026, so no science chief is recorded. No page fetched ties Patrick Gonzalez or Karen Trevino to the SEKI Biosphere Reserve; Gonzalez's Berkeley profile and ORCID confirm his own titles and are used only to enrich his person record (no new affiliation added).

FWS refuge pages list no staff names. Refuge manager taken from a KRIS-TV news story published 2024-05-06 (not an official page), so confidence is low; current status as of 2026 unconfirmed. [verifier] Re-fetched 2026-10-22: story datePublished 2024-05-06; currency in 2026 unconfirmed, kept low.

Refuge is a unit of the Big Island NWR Complex; FWS pages list no staff names. Interim manager Springer Kaye named by Hawaii Public Radio (Nov 20, 2025). Former deputy refuge manager Donna Ball (2020-2025, retired) from the Friends of Hakalau Forest board page and a 2024 FWS story. USGS research statistician Rick Camp co-analyzed the refuge's three-decade forest bird survey record (FWS story). [verifier] Rick Camp link rests on a dated May 2024 FWS story about a completed analysis: downgraded to low, is_current=false. Kaye/Hamren roles from a Nov 2025 news story only (low).

NOAA oceanservice.noaa.gov/sentinelsites/ URLs now redirect to seagrant.noaa.gov/Our-Work/RCE (no site content). The Chesapeake Bay Sentinel Site Cooperative coordinator is hosted by Maryland Sea Grant; current coordinator Taryn Sudol; first coordinator Sarah Wilkins (hired 2015). Suggested facility URL: https://www.mdsg.umd.edu/node/4324

Hawaiian Islands Sentinel Site Cooperative (HISSC) is coordinated jointly by University of Hawaii Sea Grant and NOAA Office for Coastal Management; HISSC page (c) 2026 names Katy Hintzen as Cooperative Coordinator. Suggested facility URL: https://seagrant.soest.hawaii.edu/coastal-and-climate-science-and-resilience/ccs-projects/hissc/

people.name: Anne Pfaff
people.bio: Network Program Manager for the NPS Sierra Nevada Inventory & Monitoring Network, returning to the Park Service after more than 25 years with USGS, where she was an ecologist and later research coordinator at the Sequoia-Kings Canyon Field Station working on forest and fire ecology projects across California.
people.research_interests: landscape-scale conservation; broad-scale natural resource management; forest and fire ecology

people.name: Sarah Wakamiya
people.bio: Data Manager for the NPS Sierra Nevada Network since 2021, building applications and workflows that store, analyze and share monitoring data; has served over a decade as an Inventory & Monitoring data manager, earlier with the Mid-Atlantic, Northern Great Plains and San Francisco Bay Area networks. Holds an M.S. in wildlife ecology.

people.name: Kelly Martin
people.bio: Physical Scientist with the NPS Sierra Nevada Network since 2024, leading water-resources monitoring of network lakes, rivers and wetlands; previously held ecology and physical-science positions at several western national parks. Master's in biology from CSU Fresno with an alpine-lake ecotoxicology focus.
people.research_interests: water resources monitoring; alpine lakes and wetlands; ecotoxicology

people.name: Clay Jordan
people.bio: Sequoia and Kings Canyon superintendent since late 2020, selected from the deputy superintendent post at Great Smoky Mountains; a long National Park Service career in visitor and resource protection at parks including Olympic, Mount Rainier and Shenandoah.

people.name: Patrick Gonzalez
people.bio: Associate Adjunct Professor at UC Berkeley; climate change scientist and forest ecologist. Formerly the National Park Service's principal climate change scientist (2010-2021) and an assistant director at the White House OSTP; IPCC lead author whose research documents climate-driven biome shifts, wildfire carbon losses and accelerated warming in national parks.
people.research_interests: climate change; forest ecology; ecosystem carbon; wildfire; biome shifts; national parks

people.name: Joe Saenz
people.bio: Refuge Manager at Aransas National Wildlife Refuge, Texas, per 2024 news coverage in which he discussed whooping crane recovery and the refuge's expanded land-acquisition boundary.

people.name: Springer Kaye
people.bio: Interim manager of Hakalau Forest National Wildlife Refuge (USFWS) as of late 2025; first worked at the refuge as an intern in 1999.

people.name: Donna Ball
people.bio: Retired USFWS biologist and manager with 34 years of federal service; Deputy Refuge Manager of the Big Island NWR Complex 2020-2025, earlier a conservation-partnerships biologist at the Pacific Islands Fish and Wildlife Office and a refuge biologist at the Kona and Hakalau units (1998-2006).

people.name: Richard J. Camp
people.bio: Research Statistician at the USGS Pacific Island Ecosystems Research Center, Kilauea Field Station; specializes in quantitative ecology, abundance and demographic modeling, and avian ecology and conservation, including design and analysis of Pacific Island bird surveys.
people.research_interests: status and trend estimation; Bayesian inference; hierarchical modeling; spatial and temporal modeling; population dynamics modeling; avian ecology and conservation

people.name: Taryn Sudol
people.bio: Coordinator of the Chesapeake Bay Sentinel Site Cooperative, hosted by Maryland Sea Grant; works to better connect research and outreach among federal coastal reserves of the Chesapeake region, applying sea-level-rise science to coastal decisions. Holds an M.S. from the University of Maryland in conservation biology and sustainable development.
people.research_interests: sea level rise; coastal resilience; research-to-management integration across coastal reserves

people.name: Sarah Wilkins
people.bio: Inaugural Chesapeake Bay Sentinel Site Cooperative coordinator, hired in 2015 by the Maryland Sea Grant Extension Program in partnership with Maryland DNR; previously a Knauss Marine Policy Fellow at NOAA National Ocean Service headquarters.

people.name: Katy Hintzen
people.bio: University of Hawaii Sea Grant extension agent in coastal resilience and coordinator of the Hawaiian Islands Sentinel Site Cooperative; also liaises on climate adaptation services for the Pacific Islands CASC and coordinates projects and partners for Sea Grant's Ulana Ike center. Previously worked on Great Lakes resilience with Michigan Sea Grant.
people.research_interests: coastal hazards; sea-level rise adaptation; climate adaptation; community-researcher partnerships
